To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
physical exercise and treatment with antidepressants induce a specific increase of the exon 6 variant of BDNF protein in CA3 dendritic spines.
antidepressants and physical exercise induce local increase of brain-derived neurotrophic factors (BDNF) in CA3 neurons, which may contribute to their antidepressant effects.

1) antidepressants and exercise upregulate BDNF mRNA expression in the hippocampus, 2) the upregulated BDNF mRNA is selectively localized in CA3 dendritic compartments, 3) this selective targeting of BDNFs mRNA is accounted for by Bdnf exon 6 variant, and 4) serotonin and norepinephrin increase synaptic activity and BDNF exon6 targeting in cultured hippocampal neuron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of antidepressant action, which is based on an enhanced expression of BDNf in dendrites.
the molecular basis of the action of antidepressants, in particular with the mechanisms underlying the beneficial effect of exercise on mood.
the mechanisms by which antidepressants and exercise enhance the survival and differentiation of new neurons in the adult brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antidepressant treatment induces an increased expression of Bdnf exon 6 variant, which is selectively targeted into dendrites of CA1 and CA3 pyramidal neurons.
BDNF is not a good target to treat depression, but the BDNF splice variants are.
antidepressants and physical exercise increase the expression of BDNFs in CA3 dendritic processes, and that this is a consequence of increased synaptic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antidepressants and exercise induce a specific increase of exon 6-containing BDNF mRNA targeting in the distal dendrites of CA1 and CA3 neurons.
the BDNF spatial code may be exploited as a tool to design new antidepressants.
physical exercise or antidepressant treatments increase the levels of BDNF and induce its targeting in dendrites of hippocampal CA3 pyramidal neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial code for the BDNF splice variant is not only present in the somatodendritic domain, but is also present in the dendritic compartment.
antidepressant drugs and exercise can enhance the expression of BDNFs in dendritic spines of CA3 neurons, which are involved in the formation of new memories.
antidepressants and physical exercise increase the levels of BDNF and that this increase is spatially restricted to dendrites of CA1 and CA3 neurons.
